newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CSN seeks partners for CVRD auction.
newsitem.headline: CSN seeks partners for CVRD auction.

text.p: Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) is desperately seeking cash-rich partners to form a consortium to compete in the April 29 auction of Brazil mining giant Vale do Rio Doce, a newspaper reported Tuesday.
Financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said CSN chairman Benjamin Steinbruch was in talks with big funds and corporations that had recently chosen to invest heavily in Latin American industry.

The Gazeta list included the shareholders of Banco Garantia, Garantia Participacoes, the Suzano paper and pulp group, the Soros Fund, Japanese trading company Mitsubishi and the Brazilian engineering group Camargo Correa.
Until recently considered a strong contender in the race to buy a controlling stake of CVRD, last week CSN saw its consortium fall apart.
Brazil's largest retail bank Bradesco was forced to drop out after authorities banned it from participating because of a conflict of interest arising from its role as an adviser to the sale.
South Africa's Gencor decided against taking part in the CSN-led consortium saying it would not be in the interests of its shareholders.
With little over a month to go before the sale date, Gazeta said Brazil cement and pulp group Votorantim had put together a consortium which the market considered had the best chances of taking CVRD.
The newspaper said Votorantim was in talks with Nippon Steel and a group of Brazilian pension funds which already control 15 percent of the CVRD's voting stock.
Already firmly on-board the Votorantim consortium is the South African mining group Anglo-American and Brazilian investment bank Bozano, Simonsen of the Bozano group, Gazeta said.
Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which is managing the privatization, has set a minimum price of 26.67 reais a share or a total 2.8 billion reais for the strategic 45 stake in CVRD.
